input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right binding Client exists anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for audit/inspect/records/verify/examine returned nothing, and full reads of § 2 (Licence and Hosting Services), § 5-6 (Compensation, Documentation and Disputes), § 8 (Client covenants), § 10 (Confidentiality) and §§ 12-30 confirm the only verification mechanic runs in our favour: § 6 gives Client the right to supporting documentation for charges and to contest them. The nearest TrueLink-side right, § 8(f) ("TrueLink reserves the right at any time to implement technical mechanisms to prevent Client engaging in illegal or obscene activity or in 'spamming'"), is a preventive technical measure on TrueLink's own hosted Interface, not an audit or inspection of Client, and confers no access to Client systems or records. Nothing therefore needs frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost-allocation or system-access limits, and no walk-away risk (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote access to Client systems) is present. We do not redline: inserting the preferred or fallback audit parameters would create a TrueLink audit right that does not exist today and would weaken our position. Note for the file only: if TrueLink later seeks usage verification, we would hold at once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, TrueLink's cost absent 5% underpayment, and no direct system access.
